projects.flagshipProject: Book of Record + Financial Calculation Platform
projects.description: Wealthsimple's Book of Record and Financial Calculation Platform form the financial systems foundation that records what happens to client money and continuously turns that history into the balances, positions, returns and activity clients see across Wealthsimple products. A client places a trade, deposits or transfers money, receives a dividend or completes another financial action; the request enters through the Financial Activity Model as a validated and idempotent activity, is recorded in the ledger as authoritative accounting history, and flows through streaming calculation and materialized read models that keep client-facing state continuously updated. When a transfer, trade or account activity looks unusual, machine-learning and statistical models scored on the same financial and behavioral history can flag it for review, detect anomalies, classify reconciliation breaks and surface risk signals to operations teams through internal workflows; those decisions feed fraud detection, money-movement controls and back-office investigation while preserving traceability to the underlying financial activity. It touches the frontend layer (balances, positions, activity feeds, statements and operational interfaces), the backend layer (financial APIs, event-driven services, lifecycle processing, reconciliation and orchestration), the data/AI layer (streaming calculations, financial features, anomaly detection, predictive models and model evaluation), the infrastructure layer (cloud deployment, containers, scalable processing, CI/CD and observability), and the security/governance layer (financial correctness, access controls, auditability, data protection and regulated financial controls).

Suncore, then operating as Sunroc Corporation, was modernizing the software and data workflows supporting its construction and materials businesses across the Intermountain West. The initiative connected customer and sales workflows with estimating, quoting, project and job-cost information, dispatch and fleet telemetry, materials operations, billing, and enterprise reporting so field and office teams could work from one consistent view of operational data instead of systems that had grown up separately. Cloud-based customer and operational platforms brought mobile access to crews and sales staff, while construction ERP capabilities carried project management, cost control, procurement and financial workflows. The hard problems were integrating field systems with corporate platforms, keeping job-cost and billing data reconcilable across sources, and making operational data trustworthy enough for teams to quote and dispatch from. It spans enterprise applications, backend integrations and APIs, operational and financial data pipelines, mobile and web workflows, reporting, reliability and security.
bullets: Built backend services and integrations that connected the cloud CRM used by sales and estimating with dispatch, telematics and job-cost systems, replacing manual re-keying between platforms that had grown up separately.

Delivered quoting and project workflows for ready-mix and construction operations, surfacing customer history and live operational data together so sales teams could price and commit work without leaving the application.
Developed data pipelines consolidating project, job-cost, materials and fleet telemetry into reporting models that gave operations and finance one reconcilable view across business units.
Built mobile-accessible field workflows and the APIs behind them so crews and dispatchers could record and retrieve operational data on site rather than routing everything through the office.

projects.description: CIBC expanded its digital banking platform through this period from traditional online banking into a major mobile financial-services channel, launching Canada's first mobile banking application from a major bank in 2010 and then extending it across additional devices, brokerage, mobile web, tablet banking, payments and mobile cheque deposit. Clients could view accounts, transfer funds, pay bills, move money between people, access investing, and increasingly complete banking end to end from a phone. Supporting that required integration between client applications and core banking services, transaction and payment workflows, account and balance data, authentication and authorization, fraud and security controls, and the shared digital-channel services behind every banking experience. The hard problems were availability and correctness on money movement, securing a channel that was new to the bank, and evolving customer-facing applications on top of core systems that could not move at the same pace.
bullets: Built client-facing banking applications and the digital-channel services behind them as CIBC extended from online banking into mobile, covering account access, transfers, bill payment and person-to-person money movement.

Developed integration layers between customer applications and core banking systems, isolating channel development from mainframe release cycles so new digital-channel features could evolve without waiting on core-system release cycles.
Implemented authentication, authorization and transaction security controls for a channel that was new to the bank, working within the audit and regulatory requirements of Canadian retail banking.
Delivered payment and transaction workflows with the availability and correctness guarantees money movement demands, including reconciliation and failure handling on client-initiated transfers.
